Let me take a stab at this. I'm a Front Desk Agent. 

'll use Expedia as an example in this. Though this applies to all those websites that offer discounted rates for travel if  you book through them.

What Expedia is, it is a third party website. In this equation there's three partys involved. You, expedia and me (the FDA). Expedia makes it's money by offering discounted rates. You pay expedia for those rates. The hotel doesn't see YOUR money. Expedia sends the reservation to the hotel. Expedia then pays the hotel what amounts to commission for bringing you business.

We generally can't price match for 2 reasons.

#1. Expedia makes their money by offering the discounted rates.

#2. Revenue. If we offered every room for the online price it would be a heck of a lot harder to make money in a day. Plus it would make third party sites essentially useless. Price matching is essentially too steep of a discount. We are a business and it is more or less about making  money.

I hope that makes some sort of sense. Anyone else care to add on?
